selection.reason: A clear single cardinal course, with detached framing rules omitted.
A clear single cardinal course, with detached framing rules omitted.
A meander alternates with separate four-pane square motifs; a multiple-component and joint read is needed.
The orange design contains visible crossing/contact sites. Ink alone does not specify through-routing versus joined flow.
Repeated inward square spirals have finite ends; joining them into one periodic pen course would invent connections.
Nested square outlines and grouped spiral motifs require separate components; colour may also distinguish their ownership.
The continuous upper rail meets several stems. This resembles the opposed-hook family but is not the same single-course graph.
Curved scrolls with a common baseline need curved carriers and explicit contact interpretation.
The angular interlock has crossing/contact sites whose flow routing is not established by the raster.
Diagonal crosses and diamond openings exceed the cardinal-only course grammar; crossings also need a routing read.
A clear square-wave course between detached border rules.
The familiar interlocking course is visible, but continuous outer rails meet it. The standalone interlock control does not represent those extra contacts.
Leaves and closed curved lobes share a central stem; this is a branching, curved, multiple-component construction.
Angular crossing motifs and detached dots need multiple pens and an explicit crossing interpretation.
A narrow interlocking course appears inside attached framing. The framing contacts are outside the standalone course read.
A row of finite square spirals needs start/stop pens and separate components, rather than an invented continuous course.
Curved rosettes, lattice joints, and surrounding cells require an area and multiple-course analysis.
Diagonal latticework and curved enclosed lobes exceed the cardinal single-course grammar.
A diagonal zigzag against a filled band needs diagonal carriers and separate foreground/background scope.
Several diagonal crossing courses require a multiple-pen and crossing-aware observer.
A Greek-key-like course follows a curved band; preserving its local frame requires a curved carrier rather than flattening the image silently.
Curved feather leaves are outside this line-course reader.
Interwoven curved ribbons require curve and over/under interpretation.
Paired curved spirals and corner ornaments have separate ends and components.
A clear standalone instance of the previously analyzed interlocking fret; reuse the existing idealization rather than count it as a new family.
The angular braid includes diagonal segments and over/under breaks, requiring separate course identities.
Paired curved leaves around a stem need a branching curved construction.
Filled curls and detached circles require area, curve, and multiple-component reads.

scope: Idealized cardinal courses with connected Gojo move sources. Complete descriptors use one periodic bay; material continuity and collisions use two repeats. Scorecard features overlap and are not independent votes for beauty.
